sections.heading: C - Driver Licenses and ID Cards
sections.markdown:
## C - Driver Licenses and ID Cards

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Florida residency means domiciling here over six straight months, registering to vote, or filing domicile or homestead papers [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
Immigrants are lawful permanent residents admitted by visa or USCIS adjustment, non-immigrants enter only briefly for a stated purpose, and citizens were born here or naturalized [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Residents must carry a Florida license on public roads, working or schooling newcomers within 30 days, while licensed visitors sixteen and up, federal crews, service families, and commuters are excused [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A02
College students, home-licensed migrant workers, and brief tractor or road-machine operators are also exempt [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A02
Valid licenses from listed states, Canada, France, Taiwan, and Korea waive both Class E exams, German ones waive skills, vision still applies, and kept Canadian cards force testing [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A02
Class E covers non-commercial vehicles under 26,001 pounds; motorcycles over 50 cc need an endorsement [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A02
Commercial licenses govern 26,001-plus-pound rigs, sixteen-plus-passenger carriers, and placarded hazmat with vetting [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A03
Applicants show primary identification, Social Security or secondary proof, and two address documents, all original, with a marriage, divorce, or court paper bridging name changes [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A03
Citizens identify by government birth certificate, passport or card, consular report, or naturalization or citizenship certificate [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A03
Immigrants show green cards, passport stamps, or asylum or refugee grants; Canadians and non-immigrants show parallel papers [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A04
Students add I-20 forms, exchange visitors DS-2019 forms, refugees extra papers, and travel, parole, and judge-order papers each ride with a passport [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A04
Non-citizens may draw a 60-day photo-free temporary permit while agencies verify papers, denied if verification fails [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A04
Social Security numbers are collected and verified; cards, W-2 forms, full-number paychecks, 1099 forms, or military IDs prove them [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A05
Numberless citizens and immigrants, plus all non-immigrants, supply one secondary item spanning licenses, military and school records, birth transcripts, seasoned life policies, draft and voter cards, court papers, foreign IDs, and weapon permits [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A05
Two address proofs come from leases, voter, vehicle, or vessel records, statements, utility hookups, booklets, service or medical cards, or insurance papers [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A06
Transcripts, professional licenses, tax forms, exchange certificates, shelter letters, bank and government mail, and offender forms also prove address, and housed applicants add a host letter [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A06
Learners must be 15, trained, and vision- and knowledge-tested; drivers must be 16, identified, and skills-tested too [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A06
Drivers under eighteen must hold a learner license for twelve months or until turning eighteen, whichever comes first, go twelve months without moving-violation convictions except one withheld adjudication, log at least fifty driving hours including ten at night certified by a parent, guardian, or responsible adult twenty-one or older, submit parental consent, and maintain school attendance [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A06
The substance-abuse course binds every never-licensed applicant, except certified school driver-education graduates [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A07
Unmarried minors need a signed parental application whose signer accepts responsibility and may rescind it to cancel; married and emancipated minors show certificates or court orders instead [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A07
Drivers must disclose impairing conditions, secure a doctor report for seizures or blackouts, and may mark insulin dependence [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A08
Defying a restriction draws a citation and suspension; letter codes cover lenses, hand controls, mirrors, daylight, and work limits [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A08
Numbered codes order business-only routes, interlocks, alert bracelets, automatic gears, power steering, signals, grips, pedals, and hearing aids [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A09
ID cards start at age 5, run 4 years for young holders and 8 beyond, never coexist with a license, and go free to qualifying homeless and poverty-level applicants [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A09
Career offenders register in person within 2 working days and repeat at every renewal and address or name change [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A09
Males 18 to 26 must meet draft registration, and sexual offenders and predators must register within 48 hours [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A10
Offender cards print the statute tag and predator cards the predator label, and both groups report renewals and 48-hour changes [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A10
Donor registration, free veteran marks with discharge papers, and voluntary trust-fund gifts attach at application [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A10
Address moves need a new license within 30 days via portal or office, and name changes ride on marriage, divorce, or court papers [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A11
Social Security, immigration, and Canadian passport records must be corrected before Florida reissues a renamed card [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A11
Lost cards are replaced promptly in person or online, free for theft victims bearing a police report [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A11
Full document sets return for anyone unissued since January 1, 2010, and non-immigrants renew and replace only in person [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A11
A Class E driver license remains valid for six to eight years; renewal requires presenting your old license and passing a vision exam, and is denied if you are ineligible, left a traffic summons unanswered, hold a suspended, revoked, or canceled license, or fail to present required documentation [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A12
Citizens and immigrants renew online for 6 or 8 years unless remote-renewed before or disqualified, and late filings past the birthday deadline add $15 [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A12
Drivers 80 and older pass vision screening at no charge in person or by practitioner form before renewing [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A12
First licenses, learner permits, and renewals cost $48; replacements and ID cards cost $25; late renewals add $15 [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A13
Reinstatement costs $180 for fraud, $130 for substance offenses, $75 after revocation, $45 after suspension, $60 for most lapses, and $55 for bad checks [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A13
Insurance lapses cost $15 for liability and $150, $250, then $500 across PIP suspensions inside three years, DUI cases included [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A13
Knowledge retests cost $10, skills retests $20, endorsements $7, and collector service $6.25; fully disabled veterans pay no license or ID fees [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0023]
